# Inside the Disruptive New World of Prediction Markets with Edwin Dorsey

First listed: 2026-09-30 | Evaluation cutoff: 2026-11-10

[Back to library](../README.md)

## Source versions

- [Substack: Inside the Disruptive New World of Prediction Markets with Edwin Dorsey](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/inside-the-disruptive-new-world-of) - 2026-09-30

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Dorsey argues prediction exchanges improve information, distribution and hedging, threaten sportsbooks, and may eventually replace parts of insurance. Eisman shifts from skepticism to explicit enthusiasm. Contract mechanics and Robinhood distribution are documented, but superior forecasting and low insider-trading risk remain unproven. Kalshi-only-US eligibility and Left conviction-count claims are wrong. The discussion also understates the deception theory of Left's prosecution and blurs a soldier's charges with a completed penalty. Insurance disruption has a genuine long horizon and acknowledged basis risk.

Strong conceptual distinction between trading an event and a correlated proxy, but numerous legal, access, taxation and competitive assertions need qualification. DraftKings has its own expanding prediction business, complicating the extinction analogy. Eisman's final endorsement is recorded separately from guest claims.

## Framework and tools

- Compare forecasts against realistic alternatives rather than perfection.
- Separate vote share from probability of victory.
- Specify resolution criteria before assessing event contracts.
- Distinguish direct event hedges from asset proxies and geographic basis risk.
- Do not equate enforcement anecdotes with total insider incidence.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- Binary yes/no contract prices and $1 payouts
- Weekly volume and sports/non-sports mix
- Polling and market-implied probabilities
- Fees and bid-ask spreads
- Courtroom stock charts and split adjustment
- Sportsbook versus exchange economics
- Event-triggered hurricane insurance examples
